findings.title: SSRF bypass via alternate IPv6-embedded-IPv4 encodings (6to4, NAT64) not covered by the new mapped-address check
findings.problem: The new check only unwraps `addr.ipv4_mapped` (the `::ffff:a.b.c.d` form) to catch embedded loopback/link-local/unspecified/multicast IPv4 addresses. Other standard IPv6 encodings that embed an IPv4 address are not unwrapped and sail through unchecked: 6to4 addresses (`2002:7f00:0001::/48`, exposed via `.sixtofour`) and the NAT64 well-known prefix (`64:ff9b::/96`, RFC 6052) which embeds the IPv4 address in the low 32 bits with no special accessor. For example `64:ff9b::7f00:1` decodes to 127.0.0.1 but `ip_address('64:ff9b::7f00:1').is_loopback` is False and `.ipv4_mapped` is None, so it is treated as an ordinary global IPv6 address and the URL is accepted. If Triggarr (or an intermediary resolver/proxy) ever performs NAT64/6to4 translation, or if an attacker-controlled *arr URL uses one of these forms and the underlying HTTP client / OS resolver treats it as a route to the embedded IPv4 host, this reintroduces the loopback/link-local SSRF the surrounding code is explicitly trying to close (per the `D-10` comment).
findings.fix_hint: also check addr.sixtofour and, for the 64:ff9b::/96 NAT64 prefix, extract the trailing 32 bits as an IPv4Address and apply the same is_link_local/is_loopback/is_unspecified/is_multicast test; consider a shared helper that tries all known embedding forms
findings.why_it_matters: SSRF protection is exactly the kind of control where partial coverage is dangerous: an attacker who knows the check only unwraps `::ffff:`-mapped addresses can pick a different IPv6 encoding of the same forbidden target and reach cloud metadata endpoints, loopback services, or internal-only management ports.

findings.title: IPv4-mapped IPv6 block is dead code — outer check already catches every case
findings.problem: CPython's IPv6Address.is_loopback/is_link_local/is_multicast/is_unspecified already delegate through ipv4_mapped, so the outer condition on line 82 returns for every address the new block tests. Verified empirically on Python 3.11.14 (the pyproject `requires-python = ">=3.11"` floor) and 3.14.5: `::ffff:127.0.0.1` reports is_loopback=True, `::ffff:169.254.169.254` is_link_local=True, `::ffff:224.0.0.1` is_multicast=True, `::ffff:0.0.0.0` is_unspecified=True. Removing the block and diffing validate_arr_url across all eight relevant URLs produces byte-identical results. The four new tests at tests/test_validation.py:93-109 pass with the block deleted, so they assert the outer check's behavior, not this code's.
findings.fix_hint: Delete the block as redundant, or keep it only if it is extended to cover checks the outer condition genuinely misses (see bugs-002).
findings.why_it_matters: Unreachable code implies coverage that does not exist. The D-10 comment tells a future reader IPv4-mapped addresses get special handling, so the real gap in bugs-002 reads as already-solved and is unlikely to be revisited.

findings.title: BLOCKED_HOSTS metadata IPs bypassed via IPv4-mapped IPv6 form
findings.problem: BLOCKED_HOSTS (line 18) is matched as a raw string against parsed.hostname, so it only fires on the literal decimal form. The new block re-checks the same four stdlib properties instead of the blocklist, leaving the Alibaba metadata IP reachable in mapped form: validate_arr_url("http://[::ffff:100.100.100.200]:7878") returns (True, "") while the bare "http://100.100.100.200:7878" is correctly blocked. Confirmed by direct execution. (169.254.169.254 happens to be caught anyway, but by is_link_local, not by the blocklist.)
findings.fix_hint: In the ipv4_mapped branch, compare str(mapped) against BLOCKED_HOSTS (and apply the same normalization to the bare-IP path) rather than repeating the stdlib property checks.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the SSRF hole the D-10 hardening was meant to close: an operator-supplied URL can still reach a cloud metadata endpoint by writing it in IPv4-mapped IPv6 notation.

findings.title: BLOCKED_HOSTS string matching is bypassed by the IPv4-mapped IPv6 form of metadata IPs

intent_doc_match.quote: validate the mapped address against the same blocklist

findings.problem: BLOCKED_HOSTS at line 18 is checked at line 77 by exact string comparison against parsed.hostname. The new ipv4_mapped branch (lines 85-88) only re-checks ipaddress attribute flags on the mapped address; it never re-checks the mapped address against BLOCKED_HOSTS. Verified by running the changed function: `http://[::ffff:100.100.100.200]:7878` returns (True, '') — the Alibaba metadata endpoint, which the direct form `http://100.100.100.200` correctly rejects (tests/test_validation.py::test_alibaba_metadata_blocked). The AWS/GCP metadata IP 169.254.169.254 happens to still be caught, but only incidentally via is_link_local, not via BLOCKED_HOSTS — so the class of bypass is real and BLOCKED_HOSTS is effectively dead for every mapped-form input. Any future addition to BLOCKED_HOSTS (a new cloud metadata IP that is not link-local) inherits this hole silently. This is the exact SSRF-bypass class SHIELD-007 was filed to close, reintroduced one layer down. The URL flows to triggarr/startup.py:130 as httpx `base_url=cfg.url`, so a validated URL is a URL the daemon will actually fetch with the configured API key attached.
findings.fix_hint: In the ipv4_mapped branch, also test `str(mapped) in BLOCKED_HOSTS` alongside the four attribute flags — or normalize to the mapped address once and run the single existing blocklist path over it.
findings.why_it_matters: The stated purpose of D-10/SHIELD-007 is that mapped addresses are validated against the same blocklist as direct addresses. Right now half the blocklist (the hostname set) does not apply to mapped input, so a cloud metadata endpoint reachable only by IP-string match is reachable through the ::ffff: form.

findings.title: IPv4-compatible IPv6 (::127.0.0.1) and NAT64 (64:ff9b::) embeddings are not covered by the ipv4_mapped check

intent_doc_match.quote: Plan 59-02 enumerates exactly the ::ffff: cases and only those

findings.problem: `IPv6Address.ipv4_mapped` is None for the deprecated IPv4-compatible form (::127.0.0.1) and for NAT64/WKP addresses (64:ff9b::7f00:1), and neither form sets is_loopback. Verified by running the changed function: `http://[::127.0.0.1]:7878` -> (True, '') and `http://[64:ff9b::127.0.0.1]:7878` -> (True, ''), while ipaddress.ip_address('::127.0.0.1').is_loopback is False and .ipv4_mapped is None. Whether these are actually exploitable depends on the resolver/stack in the deployment container — on many modern stacks ::x.x.x.x is not routed, which is why this is low, not medium. Sibling attributes ipaddress exposes but this code does not consult: is_reserved, is_site_local, and the 6to4/Teredo embeddings.
findings.fix_hint: If closing this, extend the extraction beyond .ipv4_mapped to also cover .sixtofour / .teredo and the ::a.b.c.d compat form; otherwise record it explicitly as risk-accepted alongside D-16/D-17 in 59-CONTEXT.md.
findings.why_it_matters: SHIELD-007 is a bypass-class finding; closing one embedding form while three others remain leaves the finding partially open. Either closing it or writing it down as accepted turns an unknown into a decision.
